All other tests pass. This confirms a genuine bug: `CSVFormat.Builder.setNullString(String)` precomputes `quotedNullString` using whatever quote character happens to be set *at that moment*, instead of deriving it from the final quote character when the format is built. If `setQuote` is called after `setNullString` in the builder chain (a perfectly reasonable, order-independent use of a builder), the quoted representation of the null string is wrong — e.g. `MYSQL.builder().setNullString("NULL").setQuote('"').setQuoteMode(QuoteMode.ALL).get()` prints `null` literally concatenated around `NULL` (`"nullNULLnull"`) instead of `"NULL"` for a null value with `QuoteMode.ALL`.

## Summary

I added `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java` with 76 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering predefined formats, `Builder` validation (line-break rejection, delimiter/quote/escape/comment collisions, `QuoteMode.NONE` without escape), duplicate-header modes, defensive copying of header/comment arrays, `equals`/`hashCode`, `toString`, `format`/`print`/`println`/`printRecord`, `parse`, deprecated `with*` methods, and several package-private helpers.

75 of the 76 tests pass. The one failing test, **`testNullStringQuotedRegardlessOfSetterOrder`**, shows a real bug:

- **Bug**: `CSVFormat.Builder.setNullString(String)` eagerly computes `quotedNullString` as `quoteCharacter + nullString + quoteCharacter` using whatever quote character is set at the time of the call, rather than at `build()` time. If `setQuote` is called *after* `setNullString` on the same builder, the final format's `QuoteMode.ALL` printing of a `null` value uses the stale (possibly absent) quote character. Example: `CSVFormat.MYSQL.builder().setNullString("NULL").setQuote('"').setQuoteMode(QuoteMode.ALL).get()` prints `nullNULLnull` instead of the expected `"NULL"`.
